card.statement:
Note that, if we denote by $\mathbf{Bun}^{\sharp}_{\mathcal{F}}$ the stack on $(\mathsf{Aff}/X,\mathrm{fppf})$ associated to the prestack $\mathbf{Bun}_{\mathcal{F}}$, we get by Remark 2.8 that in general $\underline{\mathbf{Bun}}^{\sharp}_{\mathcal{F}}\cancel{\simeq}{}_{s}u(\mathbf{Bun}^{\sharp}_{\mathcal{F}})$ in $\mathsf{St}_{k}$, unless $\mathbf{Bun}_{\mathcal{F}}$ is already a stack.

Given a map of fiber functors over $X$

$\mathring{\mathcal{F}}\longrightarrow\mathcal{F}$

there is an induced natural tranformation

$\mathbf{Bun}_{\mathcal{F}}\longrightarrow\mathbf{Bun}_{\mathring{\mathcal{F}}}$

given by restriction of bundles, and we can consider the fiber product

$\mathbf{Gr}^{\mathring{\mathcal{F}}\to\mathcal{F}}:=\mathbf{Bun}_{\mathcal{F}}\times_{\mathbf{Bun}_{\mathring{\mathcal{F}}}}\{*\}\,\,\,\in\mathsf{PSt}(\mathsf{Aff}/X).$

If the morphism between the fiber functors $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathring{\mathcal{F}}$ is implicit, we will simply use the notation $\mathbf{Gr}^{(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}})}\in\mathsf{PSt}(\mathsf{Aff}/X)$. If $u:\mathsf{Aff}/X\to\mathsf{Sch}_{k}$ is the forgetful functor, using again Definition 2.5, we put

(2.2)

$\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}^{(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}})}:=\underline{\mathbf{Gr}^{(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}})}}={}_{p}u({\mathbf{Gr}}^{(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}})})\,\,\,\in\mathsf{PSt}_{k}\qquad\qquad\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}^{(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}}),\sharp}:=(\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}^{(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}})})^{\sharp}\,\,\,\in\mathsf{St}_{k}.$

We will refer to $\mathbf{Gr}^{(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}})}$, $\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}^{(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}})}$ and $\underline{\mathbf{Gr}}^{(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}}),\sharp}$ as the Grassmannians associated to the pair of fiber functors $(\mathcal{F},\mathring{\mathcal{F}})$. In particular, we will now use the fiber functors introduced in Section 2.1 to define geometrically meaningful Grassmannians, and then compare them to the 2-dimensional Grassmannians of Definition 1.5 (see Theorem 2.14).
card.label: Remark 2.9

paper.title: Two dimensional versions of the affine Grassmannian and their geometric description
paper.abstract: For a smooth affine algebraic group $G$ over an algebraically closed field, we consider several two-variables generalizations of the affine Grassmannian $G(\!(t)\!)/G[\![t]\!]$, given by quotients of the double loop group $G(\!(x)\!)(\!(y)\!)$. We prove that they are representable by ind-schemes if $G$ is solvable. Given a smooth surface $X$ and a flag of subschemes of $X$, we provide a geometric interpretation of the two-variables Grassmannians, in terms of bundles and trivialisation data defined on appropriate loci in $X$, which depend on the flag.
